title: embeddings-rerank-incident-scratch
content:
Summary / why I’m writing this
- Observed intermittent failures on the /v1/rerank endpoint between Nov 10–Nov 12 (spike repeated Jan 5). Two symptom clusters: 1) dimension mismatch errors when scoring with embeddings from upstream embed service; 2) transient latency spikes (~1.5–3s p95 -> 6–10s) leading to timeouts in downstream clients. This doc is a scratchpad of commands, logs, hypotheses and next steps.

Timeline (high level)
- 2025-11-10 14:22 PST — first customer report (internal) of errors from rerank via hosted API.
- 2025-11-10 15:05 PST — noticed error rate bump in metrics (rerank 500s) correlated to embed requests returning 0-dim?
- 2025-11-11 — did quick hotfix to validate dims in rerank service before scoring (return 400 to caller if dims mismatch). Reduced customer 500s but root cause unknown.
- 2026-01-05 — recurrence: latency spike and occasional 400/dim mismatch in prod for a small subset of traffic routed to cluster r-45.

Observed behaviors / error snippets
- Example error logged by rerank service:
  ERROR rerank::service - embedding dimension mismatch: expected=768 actual=0 request_id=req_01F8X3M5ZT1 
  stack=rerank::scoring:45 rerank::validate:22
- Another pattern: embeddings returned with shape but NaNs:
  WARN embeddings-client - received embedding with NaN at idx 123, model=open-embed-768-v1, input_id=msg_883
- Latency trace excerpt (Jan 05, cluster r-45):
  trace_id=tr_9b3
  - embed service RPC: start 00:00:00.000 -> end 00:00:00.180 (ok)
  - rerank preprocess: start 00:00:00.181 -> end 00:00:00.190
  - scoring (matrix mult): start 00:00:00.191 -> end 00:00:06.202 (6.011s) 
  - total: 6.5s -> timed out by gateway at 6s

Commands I ran / quick repro attempts
- Curl to rerank endpoint with smaller payload:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rerank-v1","query":"q","candidates":["a","b"]}' 
  -> sometimes returns 500 with the dimension mismatch error above.

- Local python repro using embedding client mock:
  python -c "from embeddings import Client; c=Client(); e=c.embed(['a','b']); print(e.shape)"
  -> consistent 768 dims locally.

- Probe the real embed service via internal admin endpoint to dump recent responses:
  GET https://embed-admin.internal/models/open-embed-768-v1/recent?limit=200
  -> found 7 responses with length 0 and 3 responses containing NaN entries. Timestamps match spike window.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Upstream embed service bug/regression (most likely). Evidence: direct admin query returned 0-length & NaN embeddings. Also embed RPC latency not increased in most traces, which points to content-level malformed output rather than network timeouts.
2) Serialization issue in transport layer (grpc/protobuf) when handling certain content types (e.g., extremely long input, special unicode). Maybe zero-length arrays produced by a bug in proto marshal/unmarshal when using streaming responses.
3) Memory pressure / kernel-level interference on hosts in cluster r-45 causing partial writes (less likely but fits cluster-specific recurrence).
4) Scoring matrix library bug: matrix multiplication pathway hangs on certain alignment causing long scoring times (GPU fallback -> CPU slow path). Evidence: long scoring step in trace. But why would that correlate with zero-dim outputs? Possibly independent issue triggered by same upstream traffic pattern.

What I’ve tried and results
- Injected dimension validation in rerank service (hotfix) to fail fast and return 400 instead of 500: reduced customer noise but still see latency spikes.
- Added additional logging to embeddings-client: base64 of first 16 bytes of payload, model_version, server_host, response_length. Deployed to canary (10% traffic). Logs show malformed responses from embed-7 host pool.
- Replayed problematic inputs directly to embed service admin -> reproduced 0-length embeddings 2/20. Added request_id tracing to correlate.
- Checked recent deploys: embed service had a minor PR merged 2025-11-09 that touched proto streaming handler (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-service/pull/912). Rolling back that change in stage eliminated repro.

Tentative root cause (current suspicion)
- The proto streaming handler change introduced a race when streaming chunks to the client: if a final ACK arrived while buffer length was zeroed, client received a zero-length repeated field. Intermittent because depends on timing and payload size. That explains 0-dim/NaN results. Latency spikes likely secondary: some hosts hit an execution path that falls back to CPU scoring because these malformed embeddings trigger extra validation or cause memory layout that is slow.

Immediate remediation taken
- Rolled forward the hotfix in rerank service to validate dims and return 400 with clear error message (to reduce 500s).
- Hotfix to embed service: reverted PR 912 in prod on 2025-11-12 20:40 PST; monitoring for reappearance.

Open action items / next steps
- [ ] Full postmortem draft (owner: Maya) — include timeline, root cause, impact, action items. Target: 2026-01-20.
- [ ] Add stronger contract tests on embed service for streaming proto behavior (owner: Ethan) — create test with chunk timing variation. Jira: RED-1423.
- [ ] Add end-to-end canary that validates dimensions and value sanity (no NaNs) before routing to production (owner: Riley).
- [ ] Investigate scoring timeouts: instrument BLAS/cpu/gpu path selection and add metrics to expose when fallback happens (owner: eng-serving-runtime observability).
- [ ] Consider changing rerank scoring to early-exit on small candidate sets with exact dot product (temp perf win).

Notes for follow-ups (things to check)
- Search logs for "embedding dimension mismatch" across 2025-11-01..2026-01-10 and map to cluster ids.
- Check for correlation with particular customers or payload characteristics (long documents, emojis, binary attachments).
- Look at kernel/gc logs on embed hosts that produced bad outputs (embed-7 pool) for memory pressure signs.

Random snippets / commands I might need again
- gcloud/ssh into host: gcloud compute ssh embed-7-01 --project=rw-prod --zone=us-central1-a
- admin dump (internal): curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://embed-admin.internal/models/open-embed-768-v1/recent | jq '.[] | {id: .request_id, len: (.embedding|length), nan_count: (.embedding|map(select(isnan))|length)}'
- rerank logs query in Loki: {job="rerank-service"} |= "dimension mismatch" | json | line_format "{{.request_id}} {{.expected}} {{.actual}}"

Conclusion (so far)
- Most likely root cause is embed service streaming proto regression (PR 912) that occasionally returns zero-length or NaN-containing embeddings. Reverting that PR removed repro in stage. We still need stronger tests, canaries, and additional observability to guarantee it’s fully fixed and to understand the latency spike association.

-- Maya
